source.title: Chronic nicotinamide mononucleotide supplementation elevates blood nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide levels and alters muscle function in healthy older men

preparation.intervention: Oral NMN 250 mg once daily for an intended 12 weeks
preparation.placebo: Composition not established in read sources

population: Healthy Japanese men aged at least 65, BMI 22–28, nonsmokers; no active disease; no MVA or pediatric cohort

dispensing_error.timing: Other supplement supplied at week 6, discovered after study completion
dispensing_error.analysis_action: Excluded all 22 affected week-12 datasets following the ethics committee decision; retained baseline and week-six measurements
dispensing_error.interpretation: Protocol-deviation data exclusions; not 22 adverse-event withdrawals or an intended crossover

functional_tests.gait: Central 10 m of a 16-m course; average of two measurements; Table 3 reports m/s
functional_tests.grip: Two trials per hand with Smedley digital dynamometer; highest value
functional_tests.chair: Rises in 30 seconds from an armless chair

longitudinal_tests.counts: 21 per arm at baseline and week six; 10 per arm at week 12
longitudinal_tests.type: Group-by-visit interaction; nominal exploratory uncorrected findings

change_comparisons.summary: Reported group mean changes±SD; not adjusted treatment estimates

gait.method: Table 3 footnote c: unpaired t test, no baseline adjustment

gait_endpoint_limits.limit: Endpoint separation is not adjusted treatment benefit; different populations/tests are not interchangeable.

primary_mass.posthoc_power: Authors calculate for assumed large SMI effect; not proof of adequate functional power or absence of smaller benefit

retained20_week6_counterevidence.limit: Subset exploratory uncorrected comparisons, not generalized muscle harm

hierarchy_analysis.public_registry_original_and_current: SMI primary; glucose metabolism/FMD key secondary; gait/grip/chair/NAD unlisted
hierarchy_analysis.main_methods: Broader primary objectives blood NAD and body composition; secondary aging-related functions
hierarchy_analysis.reporting_summary: SMI primary; broad secondary categories; 24 January 2022
hierarchy_analysis.multiplicity: No correction explicitly applied; all analyses exploratory
hierarchy_analysis.mmrm: Alternative when mixed model fails; group/visit/interaction fixed, unrestricted covariance described

biomarker.source_distinction: Figure 2 change comparisons differ from Supplementary Table 4 endpoint comparisons; NA/NAM endpoint differences do not imply significant change differences

safety.all_adverse_event_counts: Not supplied in complete arm-specific table
safety.interpretation: Short selected-sample tolerability; not no-AE or long-term safety proof

funding_conflicts: Mitsubishi funded/supplied NMN; three employee coauthors contributed to conceptualization; others declared none

publication_notice.bounded_check: Crossmark current, Crossref/PubMed/EuropePMC notice fields plus exact-source searches

unchanged_registered_design.population: Healthy men65orolder, BMI22-28, no smoking history, Japan
unchanged_registered_design.primary: Skeletal muscle index by bioelectrical impedance

registration_dates.interpretation: Registration/disclosure precedes reported conduct; confirms prospective registration of listed outcomes only

registry_notices_detail.hierarchy_discrepancy: Paper adds primary bloodNAD and broader secondary aging-related function; archived registry lists SMI primary and glucose/FMD key secondary only
registry_notices_detail.not_concluded: Not-listing in accessible registry does not prove posthoc invention; complete original protocol/SAP absent from these records
registry_notices_detail.reading_credit: Registry/notices only; main XML targeted identity/hierarchy/date check, not additional scientific-trial reading

comparison.other_qualified_trials: Yi 2023 and Igarashi 2026 remain separate frozen qualifications; no modifications
comparison.judgment: Additional exploratory motor signals support mixed controlled human-function comparator; dispensing error and analysis limits prevent broad restoration claim
